title: The passive 1
subtitle: Present simple, past simple and will

theory.title: The passive (present simple, past simple, will)

blocks.text: **be** in the right form + past participle

rows.example: They always invite Grandma. → Grandma **is always invited**.
They invited Uncle Adrian. → Uncle Adrian **was invited**.
They **will / won't** invite the neighbours. → The neighbours **will / won't be invited**.

rows.use: When we don't know who does something
When we don't want or need to say who does something

blocks.intro: If you are not sure how to form a passive sentence, think of the active sentence first.
items: Active: Someone **stole** my sister's bike yesterday.
The object of the active sentence (**my sister's bike**) becomes the subject of the passive.
Keep the same tense. **stole** is past simple, so we need **was**.
Passive: My sister's bike **was stolen** yesterday.

blocks.text: When the verb in a passive sentence is a phrasal verb, don't forget to include the particle.
blocks.note: They **picked up** the broken glass. → The broken glass **was picked up**.

blocks.text: Some verbs have irregular past participle forms.
blocks.note: See the irregular verb list in your notes.

exercises.title: A · Correct the verb
exercises.instruction: The words in bold are wrong. Rewrite the sentence with the correct passive or active form.

items.prompt: Every year, several prizes **are giving** to the best students.
acceptedAnswers: Every year, several prizes are given to the best students.
Every year, several prizes are given to the best students

items.prompt: When the pizza **was delivering**, it was cold.
acceptedAnswers: When the pizza was delivered, it was cold.
When the pizza was delivered, it was cold

items.prompt: You **will be telling** when you can come in.
acceptedAnswers: You will be told when you can come in.
You will be told when you can come in
You'll be told when you can come in.
You'll be told when you can come in

items.prompt: That song **doesn't played** on the radio very often, is it?
acceptedAnswers: That song isn't played on the radio very often, is it?
That song isn't played on the radio very often, is it
That song is not played on the radio very often, is it?
That song is not played on the radio very often, is it

items.prompt: Your money **was stealing** out of your bag.
acceptedAnswers: Your money was stolen out of your bag.
Your money was stolen out of your bag

items.prompt: We **haven't allowed** to use a dictionary in the exam yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: We weren't allowed to use a dictionary in the exam yesterday.
We weren't allowed to use a dictionary in the exam yesterday
We were not allowed to use a dictionary in the exam yesterday.
We were not allowed to use a dictionary in the exam yesterday

items.prompt: That film **won't have shown** in our local cinema for a long time.
acceptedAnswers: That film won't be shown in our local cinema for a long time.
That film won't be shown in our local cinema for a long time
That film will not be shown in our local cinema for a long time.
That film will not be shown in our local cinema for a long time

items.prompt: **I will be picked** up from the station on Saturday?
acceptedAnswers: Will I be picked up from the station on Saturday?
Will I be picked up from the station on Saturday

exercises.title: B · Passive forms
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct passive form of the verbs in brackets.

items.prompt: When people ___ , they are taken to the police station. (arrest)
acceptedAnswers: are arrested

items.prompt: When people are arrested, they ___ to the police station. (take)
acceptedAnswers: are taken

items.prompt: Milk ___ in the fridge. (usually / keep)
acceptedAnswers: is usually kept

items.prompt: ___ what's in next week's test? (we / tell)
acceptedAnswers: Are we told
Will we be told
are we told

items.prompt: How did people communicate over long distances before the phone ___ ? (invent)
acceptedAnswers: was invented

items.prompt: ___ to come to the party next Saturday? (you / allow)
acceptedAnswers: Are you allowed
Will you be allowed
are you allowed

items.prompt: You ___ your exam results next Monday. (give)
acceptedAnswers: will be given

items.prompt: ___ yesterday? (Aidan's bike / find)
acceptedAnswers: Was Aidan's bike found
was Aidan's bike found

exercises.title: C · Bank robbery
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct passive form of a verb from the box. Add any other words you need.

items.prompt: At ten o'clock yesterday morning, the local bank in the high street ___ .
acceptedAnswers: was robbed

items.prompt: At one minute past ten, the police ___ .
acceptedAnswers: were called
were called immediately

items.prompt: A few minutes later, the police arrived at the bank. The crime scene ___ .
acceptedAnswers: was investigated

items.prompt: At twenty past ten, the robbers' fingerprints ___ .
acceptedAnswers: were found

items.prompt: At half past eleven, the robbers ___ .
acceptedAnswers: were caught

items.prompt: Next week, they ___ to prison.
acceptedAnswers: will be sent
are going to be sent

exercises.title: D · Answer in the passive
exercises.instruction: Write a full passive sentence from the prompts.

items.prompt: cars / usually / fix / in a garage
acceptedAnswers: They are usually fixed in a garage.
They are usually fixed in a garage
Cars are usually fixed in a garage.
Cars are usually fixed in a garage

items.prompt: the next Olympic Games / hold / in Paris
acceptedAnswers: They will be held in Paris.
They will be held in Paris
The next Olympic Games will be held in Paris.
The next Olympic Games will be held in Paris

items.prompt: Oscars / usually / award / to film actors
acceptedAnswers: They are usually awarded to film actors.
They are usually awarded to film actors
Oscars are usually awarded to film actors.
Oscars are usually awarded to film actors

items.prompt: I / not / allow / to use my phone / at school
acceptedAnswers: I am not allowed to use my phone at school.
I am not allowed to use my phone at school
I'm not allowed to use my phone at school.
I'm not allowed to use my phone at school

items.prompt: I / give / a bike / for my birthday / last year
acceptedAnswers: I was given a bike for my birthday last year.
I was given a bike for my birthday last year

items.prompt: I / probably / give / a book / for my next birthday
acceptedAnswers: I'll probably be given a book for my next birthday.
I'll probably be given a book for my next birthday
I will probably be given a book for my next birthday.
I will probably be given a book for my next birthday

exercises.title: E · Similar meaning
exercises.instruction: Complete the second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning. Use a passive form.

items.prompt: Will they send the letters first class? **sent** — Will the letters ___ first class?
acceptedAnswers: be sent
Will the letters be sent first class?
Will the letters be sent first class

items.prompt: I'm not sure if they eat pizza in China. **is** — I'm not sure if pizza ___ in China.
acceptedAnswers: is eaten
I'm not sure if pizza is eaten in China.
I'm not sure if pizza is eaten in China

items.prompt: Someone told me that they don't make cars in the UK anymore. **made** — Someone told me that cars ___ in the UK anymore.
acceptedAnswers: aren't made
are not made
aren't made in the UK anymore
Someone told me that cars aren't made in the UK anymore.

items.prompt: Do they usually feed the animals three times a day? **fed** — Are the animals ___ three times a day?
acceptedAnswers: usually fed
Are the animals usually fed three times a day?
Are the animals usually fed three times a day

items.prompt: Mr Jones is ill, so he won't give us a geography test today! **be** — Mr Jones is ill, so we ___ a geography test today!
acceptedAnswers: won't be given
will not be given
won't be given a geography test today
Mr Jones is ill, so we won't be given a geography test today!

items.prompt: Did they take her to hospital in an ambulance? **she** — Was she ___ to hospital in an ambulance?
acceptedAnswers: taken
Was she taken to hospital in an ambulance?
Was she taken to hospital in an ambulance

exercises.title: F · The National Trust
exercises.instruction: Write one word in each gap.

items.prompt: There are lots of beautiful, large houses in Britain. Many of them ___ built hundreds of years ago.
acceptedAnswers: were

items.prompt: In the past, they ___ owned by very rich families.
acceptedAnswers: were

items.prompt: Today, many of them ___ owned by an organisation called The National Trust,
acceptedAnswers: are

items.prompt: which ___ created to look after them.
acceptedAnswers: was

items.prompt: The houses ___ kept in perfect condition,
acceptedAnswers: are

items.prompt: and visitors ___ allowed to look round them.
acceptedAnswers: are

items.prompt: It's interesting to learn how different life was in an old house. Milk was ___ kept in the fridge, because they didn't have fridges!
acceptedAnswers: not
never

items.prompt: Washing machines ___ only invented very recently,
acceptedAnswers: were

items.prompt: so washing ___ done by hand.
acceptedAnswers: was

items.prompt: In some cases, the house ___ still lived in today.
acceptedAnswers: is

items.prompt: When this happens, visitors ___ only shown part of the house.
acceptedAnswers: are

items.prompt: The private rooms ___ kept closed to the public.
acceptedAnswers: are

items.prompt: The gardens ___ looked after by professional gardeners.
acceptedAnswers: are

items.prompt: Members of the National Trust ___ given a discount.
acceptedAnswers: are

items.prompt: This year, millions of people ___ be given the chance to see what life in an old country house was like.
acceptedAnswers: will
